ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, UBOs, and beneficiaries against the Canadian Consolidated Automatic Sanctions List, FINTRAC guidance and sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act, the OFAC SDN List (required for USD-denominated TikTok Creator Payout and Wise B2B rails), UN Security Council sanctions, UK HMT sanctions, and global negative-media sources; foreign PEP status triggers Enhanced Due Diligence consistent with FATF Recommendations 10 and 12.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (official provincial online portal via https://www.alberta.ca/corporate-registry and the Alberta Corporate Internet Registry, with mandatory NUANS name search conducted through accredited NUANS service providers)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered corporate name must be expressed in English or French using Roman-alphabet characters; non-Latin script brands (e.g., Chinese characters or pinyin) are not accepted as the legal name. The name must include a distinctive element and a legal designator, being 'ULC' or 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' (or the French equivalent 'société à responsabilité illimitée'). A transliterated or translated trade style may be used separately under the Business Names Registration Act (Alberta), but the legal corporate name must be Roman-alphabet based and not merely descriptive.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, the applicant may: (1) amend the proposed name and file a fresh NUANS report demonstrating distinctiveness; (2) file a written reconsideration request to the Director of Corporate Registry within 30 days, attaching legal argument on name-permissibility under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) and regulations; (3) if the Director confirms refusal, apply for judicial review to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the Alberta Rules of Court. Given 'TikTok' and 'ByteDance' are third-party trade-marks, the applicant must either obtain a written trade-mark consent from the owner or replace the brand token with a coined distinctive element; failure to do so will result in automatic NUANS rejection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual or service-office footprint is permissible for this advertising/MCN industry only if the registered agent maintains a physical street address in Alberta, is staffed during normal business hours, and accepts service of process; a mail-forwarding-only or non-physical address is rejected by the Alberta Corporate Registry and constitutes a statutory violation. The ULC must maintain its statutory records, including the UBO register, at the registered office or another prescribed location in Alberta accessible for inspection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate; estimated annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the Canada Revenue Agency (GST/HST field verification) or the Alberta Corporate Registry is 5-10%. The probability rises above 15% if the ULC's passthrough tax classification and intercompany service arrangements trigger CRA audit profiling, or if the registered agent is a high-density virtual-office provider attracting compliance sweeps.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended: s. 8 (incorporation instruments), s. 12 (articles of incorporation), s. 15.1 (unlimited liability corporation designation), s. 20 (certificate of incorporation), s. 104 (registered office), s. 129 (corporate records); the provincial incorporation fee is CAD 350 (approx. USD 260).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, operating through the Corporate Registry e-filing system and accredited Corporate Registry Agents.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) together with Notice of Registered Office (Form 2), Notice of Directors (Form 3), and the NUANS name search report.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an Alberta ULC; shares may be issued for nominal consideration and no escrow, escrow deposit, or minimum paid-in capital is required under the Alberta Business Corporations Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the Corporation adopt its Articles of Incorporation and accept the subscription for 100 Class A common shares at CAD 0.01 per share, such shares to be allotted and issued to the founding shareholder upon full payment; AND RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Corporation's registered office be established at the address shown in the Notice of Registered Office, City of Calgary, Alberta, with statutory corporate records maintained at that address; AND RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the following officers be appointed: [Name] as Chief Executive Officer, [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] as Corporate Secretary, each to serve until removed by the Board; AND RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the officers be authorized to file all statutory registrations and open commercial bank accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) through an accredited Corporate Registry Agent e-filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS (Newly Updated Automated Name Search) request through an accredited Alberta Corporate Registry agent, proposing up to three corporate names for the unlimited liability corporation, each incorporating 'Alberta' or an approved abbreviation; review the NUANS report for conflicts and reserve the preferred name for 90 days.
required_dossiers: Completed NUANS name search request form
Proposed corporate name list (up to 3 alternatives)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected for confusing similarity, file a new NUANS request with an alternative name or submit a written consent letter from the holder of the conflicting name; reserve the replacement name for the remaining statutory period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Articles of Incorporation and Statutory Notices
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) - prescribed forms unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft Form 1 (Articles of Incorporation) for an unlimited liability corporation, together with Form 2 (Notice of Registered Office) and Form 3 (Notice of Directors); the articles must expressly designate the unlimited liability class of shares, authorized share structure, transfer restrictions, and number and qualification of directors; the incorporator executes the completed instruments.
required_dossiers: Consent of directors to act in office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Upon receipt of a registry requisition, amend the defective clause or attach the missing consent and resubmit the corrected instrument through the same accredited agent within the requisition response window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of the Incorporation Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) online portal or accredited Registry Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the consolidated electronic incorporation application and the prescribed CAD 350 fee through the Corporate Registry e-filing system; the filing captures the articles, registered office notice, and directors notice in a single transaction; the filer must select the 'unlimited liability company' designation to perfect the ULC status under the ABCA.
required_dossiers: Payment of the CAD 350 incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any rejection or requisition is logged in the Corporate Registry portal; correct the identified deficiencies and re-submit within the statutory response period (generally 30 days) without an additional fee where the original filing was timely.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and CRA Business Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Alberta Corporate Registry issues the Certificate of Incorporation for the named or numbered ULC; the registry automatically transmits the corporate record to the CRA, which generates a 9-digit Business Number (BN); verify the BN in CRA My Business Account and retain the electronic proof of registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Business Number is not auto-issued within 48 hours of incorporation, contact the CRA Business Registration line at 1-800-959-5525 or submit Form RC1A to request the BN retroactively.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Program Account and Provincial Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Alberta Corporate Tax (administered by CRA under the Tax Collection Agreement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the GST/HST account (mandatory once worldwide taxable revenue exceeds CAD 30,000; voluntary registration is recommended to recover input tax credits on TikTok creator payouts), open a payroll deductions program if employees are hired, and confirm the Alberta corporate income tax account through the CRA; for cross-border US tax planning, the ULC may elect to be a disregarded entity by filing IRS Form 8832.
required_dossiers: Form RC1 - Request for a Business Number and Program Accounts
Form RC59 - Authorizing a Representative (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If program accounts are not activated within 10 business days, escalate through the CRA Business Window at 1-800-959-5525; file an objection under section 305 of the Excise Tax Act where a registration request is incorrectly refused or delayed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence, Occupancy Compliance, and Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Calgary (or City of Edmonton) Licensing and Building Safety; ProService Alberta; commercial bank (e.g. TD Canada Trust, RBC) or Wise B2B
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For a commercial office location, obtain a City of Calgary Business Licence where required by municipal by-law; secure the Alberta Fire Code occupancy permit through a fire safety inspection; and open the corporate operating account, presenting the Certificate of Incorporation, Business Number, and the board resolution appointing bank signatories; alternatively activate the Wise B2B multi-currency treasury balance for TikTok creator payouts and supplier remittances.
required_dossiers: Board resolution on bank account signatories
Lease agreement or proof of registered office occupancy
City of Calgary Business Licence application (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire or building occupancy inspection identifies deficiencies, submit a corrective action plan to the Safety Codes Council for re-inspection; if bank onboarding triggers enhanced due diligence, provide the current corporate registry extract, ULC shareholder schedule, and source of funds declaration for the founder capital contribution.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Municipal Affairs (Safety Codes Council) and City of Calgary Planning and Building Safety; no sector-specific industrial licensing regime applies to ISIC 7310 advertising or MCN agency services.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no mandatory operating license; optional City of Calgary Business Licence (General Office/Business Services) may apply to the physical office location.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category 1 (no Environmental Impact Assessment required; office-based administrative services do not trigger the Schedule of Activities under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-12)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source wastewater discharge, VOC, or hazardous waste compliance thresholds for the office operation; general waste must be disposed of through municipal collection; electronic waste, if generated in volume, must be handled through Alberta Recycling Management Authority approved facilities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Alberta Fire Code (Safety Codes Act) fire safety clearance for the office occupancy class; structural load and occupant load inspection under the National Building Code - Alberta Edition; Alberta Occupational Health and Safety (OHS Act and OHS Code) workplace clearance, including emergency exit signage, first aid equipment, and ergonomic workstations for creator operations staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — Business Registration Online (BRO) portal: https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses.html
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities establishing a Canada/ULC branch or corporation must first complete federal incorporation or extra-provincial registration with Corporations Canada (or the Alberta Corporate Registry for AB-ULC), then obtain a Canada Revenue Agency Business Number (BN) via online registration or Form RC1. The BN serves as the GST/HST registration number, corporate income tax account, payroll, and import/export account. Non-resident corporations that carry on business in Canada and have Canadian-source revenues must apply for a BN before commencing activities. There is no separate TIN; the 9-digit BN plus two-letter program account code (e.g., RT for GST/HST) is used. ULCs with unlimited liability are treated as corporations under Canadian tax law and are subject to the same BN process. Registration must be completed within 30 days of becoming a registrant. Supporting documents include certificate of incorporation, articles, proof of registered office address, and a completed Form RC464 for non-resident businesses if applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (ULC is taxable as a corporation under the Canadian Income Tax Act; despite its unlimited liability, it is not a pass-through entity for Canadian federal/provincial corporate income tax purposes. For U.S. federal tax purposes, the ULC may be treated as an entity eligible for check-the-box classification, but this does not alter its Canadian tax status.)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No Canadian check-the-box election exists; Canadian tax classification follows legal form. A ULC is mandatorily a corporate taxpayer under Part I of the Income Tax Act. However, an Alberta ULC may make an election under section 216(1) to file on a net basis as a non-resident if carrying on business in Canada. For hybrid mismatch purposes, Canada applies OECD hybrid mismatch rules per Section 815, which may deny deductions for payments involving hybrid entities, such as a ULC deemed to be a disregarded entity in another jurisdiction. The ULC's unlimited liability does not afford any Canadian tax transparency election. A ULC can also elect under subsection 256.1(1) to treat a wholly owned subsidiary as a branch for tax purposes in limited inter-corporate scenarios, but this is not analogous to check-the-box.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) / Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) — federal value-added tax; Alberta does not impose a provincial sales tax, so only the 5% federal GST applies on taxable supplies made in Alberta.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in annual worldwide taxable supplies (excluding zero-rated and certain financial services) triggers mandatory GST/HST registration. An entity may voluntarily register before exceeding the threshold; non-resident corporations carrying on a business in Canada and earning GST taxable income must register regardless of threshold if not a 'small supplier'. For non-resident digital economy suppliers, including MCN/advertising services, the threshold applies to Canadian-source digital supplies unless an election is made under the simplified non-resident registration framework (Form GST494).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate a real-time domestic e-invoicing clearance/OCR system comparable to Latin American countries. GST/HST registrants must issue periodic prescribed information in a retrievable electronic or paper format. CRA accepts electronic invoices for GST/HST purposes if the invoice contains all required information (vendor BN, date, tax rate, tax amount, amount). Digital stamping or tax authority clearance is not required. Reporting is generally done through tax returns filed electronically via GST/HST NETFILE; mandatory electronic filing applies to most registrants with annual revenues above CAD 10,000. While there is no pre-clearance API, CRA's Business Gateway API permits machine-to-machine filing of GST/HST returns and remittances, and participants in the GST/HST post-audit environment are expected to maintain structured audit files (GIFI).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% GST) applies to exports of goods from Canada (provided the goods are physically removed from Canada within a reasonable time and will not be resold in Canada) and to certain services performed on exported goods. For advertising and MCN agency services supplied to non-residents, zero-rating generally applies under section 23(1) of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act if the service is delivered to a recipient who is a non-resident of Canada and is not required to be used in Canada. Advertising services are zero-rated when supplied to non-residents except where the supply relates to advertising to a Canadian audience or is performed in a manner that would have been part of the advertiser's taxable business in Canada. For TikTok creator agency services, the key test is whether the service is supplied to a non-resident (e.g., TikTok entity) for use and consumption exclusively outside Canada; if any element is used in Canada, the supply may be taxable at 5%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A / CAED) filed through CBSA's Canadian Export Reporting System (CES), required for exports of goods with a value exceeding CAD 2,000 or controlled/prohibited goods; for services no customs declaration is filed but commercial invoices and service agreements are required.
Bill of Lading (through ocean, air, or rail carrier; for digital services a signed contract and delivery record / server access logs are acceptable in lieu of transport documents)

Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/Fintech payment proof (e.g., Wise B2B confirmation or TikTok Creator Payout summary) evidencing funds received from outside Canada in the exporter's Canadian account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and CBSA may jointly audit zero-rated export claims. Where documentation fails to establish physical export or direct foreign consumption, CRA will reassess the supply as taxable at 5%, apply interest and penalty under subsection 280(1) of the Excise Tax Act (net failure penalty of up to 6% of unpaid tax, plus a repeated-failure penalty of 8% and 4% per year compounding). Additionally, intentional misrepresentation for zero-rating may lead to a 13% civil penalty under section 285.1, and repeated serious violations constitute GST evasion subject to criminal prosecution under the Income Tax Act or Excise Tax Act with fines of up to CAD 200,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years for intentional falsification of records. Exporters must retain all substantiation in English or French for six years from the end of the audit period. If export rehearing proceeds are not repatriated within 180 days due to foreign-exchange controls, the exporter may be required to accrue revenue in Canadian dollars and may face a 10% surtax on unremitted income under ITA section 17, unless a deferral election is obtained.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); prudential oversight by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); anti-money-laundering supervision by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC); foreign-investment screening under the Investment Canada Act administered by Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully and freely convertible under a floating exchange-rate regime; there are no capital-account controls on inbound equity injections, dividend repatriation, or liquidation proceeds. Current-account transactions, including creator payouts and cross-border service fees, are unrestricted. Profit remittance is governed solely by tax at the point of outflow: 25% Part XIII withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (Canada) on dividends paid to non-residents, typically reduced under an applicable treaty (e.g., 5% under the Canada–US Treaty for a corporate owner of at least 10% voting shares). No regulatory authorization is required for remittance; only FINTRAC cross-border electronic-funds-transfer reporting applies at CAD $10,000 or above.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation period for export receipts or foreign-currency service revenues. The Alberta ULC may retain USD and other foreign currency in resident or non-resident banking accounts indefinitely. The only applicable obligations are Canadian income-tax recognition of foreign-exchange gains and losses under sections 39 and 95 of the Income Tax Act (Canada) and standard financial-reporting rules.

Capital Escrow / Share Subscription Proceeds Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High as a settlement adjunct; Medium as a primary treasury bank. Wise Business (Wise Canada Inc., registered as a Money Service Business with FINTRAC) and Payoneer provide multi-currency account equivalents and low-cost local-rail creator payouts using SWIFT-equivalent routing. Legal constraints: any non-bank EMI must be FINTRAC-registered; EMIs do not carry Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation protection, offer limited credit and FX-hedging product suites, and are generally unsuitable for holding the ULC's capital-escrow subscription account. Recommended use: sub-CAD $10,000 creator payouts and volatile-currency disbursements only.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted by all major Canadian banks for a Canadian-incorporated ULC. Directors and ultimate beneficial owners are not required to appear physically in Alberta; banks accept video-verified identity, notarized/certified corporate packets, and a bank-to-bank reference letter. Risk-calibrated exceptions may require an in-person Calgary or Edmonton visit for the signatory director where the beneficial-ownership chain or settlement-counterparty pattern is elevated. Practical expectation for a clean corporate package: two to four weeks end-to-end at Tier 1 banks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ultimate beneficial ownership: the ULC is held by a foreign parent, and no individual appears immediately at 25% or greater control.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta Business Corporations Act beneficial-ownership attestation; full corporate organizational chart extending to ultimate individuals; certified share register and minute book; directors' resolution identifying the controlling shareholder; corporate-counsel legal opinion confirming the ULC unlimited-liability structure and shareholder identification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk counterparty jurisdiction: TikTok/ByteDance settlement flows routed from Singapore, Hong Kong, or China-based treasury centers trigger sanctions and source-of-funds scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Creator Incubation and Global MCN Agency Agreement with TikTok; official settlement statements evidencing arm's-length service fees; tax residence certificates of the remitting payer where applicable; documented money-laundering risk assessment confirming the counterparty is not a designated sanctioned entity; commission-calculation sub-ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Structuring indicators: high-frequency and/or batched low-value payouts to hundreds of foreign creators resembling transaction layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master Creator Registry with KYC/KYB packages per payee; monthly payout files carrying unique invoice references; standing-instructions agreement; written compliance manual confirming the ULC performs no money-transmission services and is not an unregistered MSB; FINTRAC cross-border EFT reporting framework for transactions at CAD $10,000 or above.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth of startup capital: inbound share-subscription injection from a non-resident parent into an escrow account without clear provenance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements of the parent; share subscription agreement and directors' resolution; bank reference letter from the remitting institution; three-month source-of-funds bank statements; written confirmation of Investment Canada Act status, including assessment against the WTO-investor direct-acquisition threshold.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP screening hits on creator counterparty names and payout jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Real-time screening outputs against OSFI-administered Canadian sanctions lists, the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, and applicable UN/OFAC lists; negative-media search results; completed PEP questionnaire for affected counterparties; legal sign-off permitting onward payout where an adverse match is disproven.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inject parent capital via SWIFT MT103 credit transfer to the TD Capital Escrow / Share Subscription Account, using Remittance Information field 70: 'ULC Share Subscription – [Parent Name] – [Date]'. Include bank-to-bank information in field 72 where a correspondent intermediary is required. Canadian banks expect a purpose narrative: 'Equity contribution for working capital and creator acquisition.' Confirm Investment Canada Act non-filing status: the WTO-investor direct-acquisition threshold currently exceeds CAD $1 billion and is revised annually, and an MCN service business will ordinarily fall below it. Maintain on file: share subscription agreement; directors' resolution authorizing share issuance; updated share register; source-of-funds letter from the remitting parent bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail: SWIFT MT103 batch payouts via bank host-to-host file channels (RBC Global Payment, BMO Global Payment Plus) for creator fees and talent advances. Secondary rail for creator local-currency payouts below CAD $10,000: Wise B2B multi-currency API using local clearing rails to eliminate correspondent double-FX and reduce remittance cost. Where physical merchandise co-packing is later introduced, settle supplier invoices via Commercial Letter of Credit (SWIFT MT700) confirmed by the issuing Alberta branch; service-based MCN contracts do not require LCs. All outbound electronic funds transfers at or above CAD $10,000 require FINTRAC cross-border EFT reporting. Payouts to Canadian resident creators are reported via T4A/independent-service statements aligned with CRA requirements. Maintain a daily USD/CAD sweep between the USD settlement account and the CAD operational account governed by an OSFI-approved forward line.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CAD/USD deliverable foreign-exchange forwards, evergreen or 1–12 month maturity, executed under an ISDA Master Agreement with the hedge bank
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on non-convertible creator-payout currencies (PHP, BRL, IDR, VND) via Scotiabank or BMO NDF desks
CAD/USD cross-currency swaps for medium-term capital-structure hedging, with CORRA-based discounting per Canadian market convention

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (Form AR) filed under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) and the Corporate Registry Regulation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Alberta Registrar of Corporations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary date of incorporation or amalgamation; fixed calendar anniversary rule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A default entry is recorded after the deadline; the Registrar may administratively dissolve the corporation after two consecutive unfiled years and the expiry of the prescribed remedy period. Reinstatement requires the filing of all outstanding returns and a CAD 200 restoration fee.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (including Alberta provincial tax schedules and any required CRA financial information)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Calgary Tax Services Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; a December 31 year-end therefore requires filing by June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of any unremitted tax balance, plus 1% per complete month for up to 12 months; directors may be liable for unpaid withholdings and CRA enforcement may culminate in provincial administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements, director's report, and auditor's report (if any) laid before the shareholders at the annual general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders at the annual general meeting (corporate record; original retained in the statutory minute book at the Alberta registered office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of each fiscal year, coinciding with the ABCA annual meeting deadline of not later than 6 months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Shareholders holding at least 5% of the issued voting shares may compel an audit; non-compliance exposes the corporation to court-ordered remedial relief under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) but does not of itself trigger administrative dissolution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No general statutory audit applies to a non-reporting private corporation under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta). A mandatory independent audit attaches only if: (i) the corporation is a reporting issuer or offers securities to the public; (ii) it operates as a bank, trust company, insurance company, or other regulated financial institution; (iii) shareholders holding at least 5% of the issued voting shares demand an audit at an annual meeting; or (iv) the articles or a unanimous shareholders agreement require an audit. A private ULC creator-MCN agency is therefore ordinarily subject only to a review or agreed-upon-procedures engagement unless a covenant or shareholder resolution raises the standard.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or Canadian GAAP (ASPE) as elected under the CPA Canada Handbook; annual financial statements must be prepared and presented regardless of audit status, and the selected framework must support both the CRA T2 corporate income tax filing and any US check-the-box passthrough allocation to the ULC members.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta's corporate registry has not yet operationalized a provincial beneficial-ownership registry for ABCA corporations; therefore the ULC maintains, in the statutory minute book, an internal register of individuals with significant control (direct or indirect holders of 25% or more of voting rights or equity), updated on each share issuance or transfer. During each annual cycle, at the AGM held within six months after fiscal year-end, the board runs an internal statutory-register audit: it reconciles the register of members, share-transfer register, register of directors, and minute book against the filed Alberta Annual Return and confirms the current significant-control schedule in the AGM minutes. Any share transfer completed during the year must be recorded in the share-transfer register before the AGM, and nominee or ULC unlimited-liability holdings require written consent documentation to remain valid corporate records.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book
Register of Debentures and Bonds (if applicable)
Register of Continuing Powers of Attorney (if applicable)
